_what: The tools the Namespace tool server lists over MCP (src/serve/mcp.rs): one for each account files operation the door answers (account-files-routes.json `operations`), and `this_computer`, which the run answers itself from the computer the engine filled except `setup_facts` and `held_connections`, which the engine's account routes answered and this tool has no composition for. The server refuses to start when an operation of the routes is not listed here or a listed name is not an operation.

tools.name: list_files
tools.description: List one page of the names and folders in a folder, in name order.

folder.description: The folder path, / for the top

device.description: This device's id: each name then says whether this device keeps it (kept), by the device's pin rules

tools.name: find_file
tools.description: The facts kept about one file: identity, size, media type, where it is stored, its names.

name_or_identity.description: A file's name (a path such as /Notes/a.txt) or its content identity (1f: or 12: then 64 hex digits)

tools.name: show_file
tools.description: A file's facts and the way to open it.

name_or_identity.description: A file's name (a path such as /Notes/a.txt) or its content identity (1f: or 12: then 64 hex digits)

tools.name: file_objects
tools.description: The stored objects a file is made of (one, or one for each chunk).

name_or_identity.description: A file's name (a path such as /Notes/a.txt) or its content identity (1f: or 12: then 64 hex digits)

tools.name: files_summary
tools.description: How many files, names, chunks and bytes the person keeps, and in which store.

tools.name: usage_days
tools.description: The person's own usage counts, one row for each day.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Find files by the words in their names.

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Read up to 256 KiB of a file from an offset, as text when the bytes are UTF-8 and not an image, else as base64. Reads only the asked range from the store.

name_or_identity.description: A file's name (a path such as /Notes/a.txt) or its content identity (1f: or 12: then 64 hex digits)

offset.description: First byte to read, 0 by default

encoding.description: auto gives text for UTF-8, base64 always gives base64

upload_id.description: Read what an upload in progress holds so far

tools.name: read_file_span
tools.description: Read one exact byte range of a file, as base64.

name_or_identity.description: A file's name (a path such as /Notes/a.txt) or its content identity (1f: or 12: then 64 hex digits)

raw.description: true: the span is written as a file of its bytes as the store sends them, and the answer names it ({bytes: {file, total, offset, length, identity}}), never holding them, given as soon as its first bytes are in it; the file grows to length (emptied if the read fails after the answer); the engine hands the bytes to its caller raw (an octet stream) from the first byte and removes the file. false or absent: the bytes are in the answer as base64.

tools.name: write_file
tools.description: Keep a whole small file under a name: its text or its base64 bytes.

name.description: The name to give, a path such as /Notes/a.txt

text.description: The file's text (give this or content_base64)

content_base64.description: The file's bytes, base64 (give this or text)

media_type.description: The media type, application/octet-stream by default

expected_version.description: The version of the name (or folder) you read, from list_files, show_item or list_changes; 0 when the name must not exist yet. The write is refused with a conflict if it changed since

tools.name: write_file_start
tools.description: Begin a large file upload: declare its name and length, then send pieces and finish.

upload_id.description: A new 32 lowercase hexadecimal id for this upload

name.description: The name the file will have

byte_length.description: The file's whole length in bytes

length_known.description: false for a stream of unknown length (leave byte_length out)

app.description: What is sending it, for the record

expected_version.description: The version of the name (or folder) you read, from list_files, show_item or list_changes; 0 when the name must not exist yet. The write is refused with a conflict if it changed since

tools.name: write_file_piece
tools.description: Send one piece of an upload at its offset, as content_base64 or as content_file (exactly one).

content_base64.description: The piece's bytes, base64; or give content_file instead

content_file.description: The piece sent raw: the file of its bytes the engine put in this run's own folder (the row's session.byte_argument), {path relative to that folder, length}; it is read and removed

tools.name: write_file_finish
tools.description: Finish an upload: the file is checked against its identity and given its name.

identity.description: The identity the finished bytes must have, when known

tools.name: write_file_cancel
tools.description: Cancel an upload and keep nothing of it.

tools.name: write_file_described_spans
tools.description: Give the chunk spans a client already stored for an upload.

spans.description: The spans: offset, length and the chunk identity of each

tools.name: read_file_described_spans
tools.description: Read back the chunk spans an upload holds.

tools.name: share_file
tools.description: Make a link that opens one file or many (any size) without any other credential, for 1 up to 604800 seconds (7 days). A browser that opens it gets the share's page (each item shown and played, in the person's own look, when the share route has a page); anything else gets the first file's bytes, whole or by byte range. Each item may name other files of the person's as its forms, such as a copy every browser plays (play) or a poster (poster); the page uses them and the route serves them at <link>/<n>/<form>. The link is answered once, with its key; only a digest of the key is kept, as one row of the person's own files, read on every request, so stop_share refuses the next read.

name_or_identity.description: One file: its name (a path such as /Notes/a.txt) or its content identity (1f: or 12: then 64 hex digits). Name this or items, not both

forms.description: With name_or_identity: the file's forms, each a form's name (letters, digits, - or _) to another file of the person's, such as {"play": "/previews/clip 1080p.mp4", "poster": "/previews/clip.jpg"}

items.description: Many files at one link, in the order the page shows them: each a file's name or identity, or {name_or_identity, forms}

title.description: The words the page shows above the items (one line); without it, the first file's name

seconds.description: How long the link lasts, 1 to 604800

tools.name: stop_share
tools.description: Stop one share of a file now: the next request for its link is refused. Stopping a stopped share answers the same.

id.description: The share's id, as share_file and list_shares answer it

tools.name: list_shares
tools.description: The shares of files, a page in id order: id, name, identity, expires_at and state (open, stopped or ended). A key is never answered.

after.description: The id the page starts after

tools.name: keep_look
tools.description: Keep your own look, worn by every share page your share route draws: your name and colours, never those of whoever runs the computer. look is shaped like a site setting (name, theme {data_theme, scheme, theme_color}, look_css); null takes it away.

look.description: {name, theme: {data_theme, scheme, theme_color}, look_css}, at most 256 KiB; null takes the kept look away

tools.name: find_names
tools.description: The names in a folder that start with a prefix.

prefix.description: The start of the names to find, a folder path then the first letters

after.description: Where the last page stopped (its next_after)

limit.description: Most steps or entries in this page

tools.name: move_names
tools.description: Move a name, or a whole folder of names, to another place. Only names change: the files and their bytes stay. Answers next_after until done.

from.description: The name or folder to move

after.description: Where the last page stopped (its next_after)

limit.description: Most steps or entries in this page

expected_version.description: The version of the name (or folder) you read, from list_files, show_item or list_changes; 0 when the name must not exist yet. The write is refused with a conflict if it changed since

tools.name: copy_names
tools.description: Give a name, or a whole folder of names, a second name. Only names are added.

from.description: The name or folder to copy

after.description: Where the last page stopped (its next_after)

limit.description: Most steps or entries in this page

tools.name: set_aside
tools.description: Set a name or a whole folder aside: it leaves the file list and can be put back.

after.description: Where the last page stopped (its next_after)

limit.description: Most steps or entries in this page

expected_version.description: The version of the name (or folder) you read, from list_files, show_item or list_changes; 0 when the name must not exist yet. The write is refused with a conflict if it changed since

tools.name: put_back
tools.description: Put a set-aside name or folder back where it was.

after.description: Where the last page stopped (its next_after)

limit.description: Most steps or entries in this page

expected_version.description: The version of the name (or folder) you read, from list_files, show_item or list_changes; 0 when the name must not exist yet. The write is refused with a conflict if it changed since

tools.name: list_set_aside
tools.description: List the names set aside in a folder.

tools.name: forget_set_aside
tools.description: Forget a set-aside name or folder for good; the files nothing else names are noted for the byte release.

after.description: Where the last page stopped (its next_after)

limit.description: Most steps or entries in this page

tools.name: retire_names
tools.description: Set aside and forget temporary names by exact path and expected identity.

tools.name: queue_release
tools.description: Turn the noted files nothing holds into release rows.

tools.name: release_gone_bytes
tools.description: Remove from their stores the bytes of files that were forgotten, until the call's time ends.

tools.name: list_released
tools.description: List the storage given back.

tools.name: recent_files
tools.description: The files the person used most recently, newest first.

tools.name: record_file_use
tools.description: Note that a file was used: opened, watched, edited or published.

kind.description: What happened, one of opened, watched, edited, published

tools.name: set_file_facts
tools.description: Keep facts about a file (only the facts named change; null takes one away).

tools.name: record_file_results
tools.description: Keep results made about files, by identity and kind.

tools.name: read_file_results
tools.description: Read the results kept about a file.

tools.name: read_file_result_fields
tools.description: Read some fields of one kind of result kept about a file.

tools.name: list_file_results
tools.description: List the results of one kind across files; with no kind, the count of each kind.

tools.name: read_file_results_many
tools.description: Read one kind of result for many files at once.

tools.name: merge_file_result
tools.description: Merge a patch into a kept result.

only_if_empty.description: Only when no value is kept

tools.name: remove_file_result
tools.description: Remove one kept result.

tools.name: list_changes
tools.description: The changes to the person's names and folders after a cursor, in the store's own order: each {op: put|remove, kind: name|folder, item, generation} and, for put, the row as list_files gives it. Without after it answers only next, the cursor of now. A rename is one put of the same item.

after.description: A cursor an earlier list_changes answered (next)

wait.description: true: when nothing changed after the cursor, wait for a change until the call's own time ends

device.description: This device's id: each name then says whether this device keeps it (kept), by the device's pin rules

tools.name: show_item
tools.description: The live name or folder that holds a stable item id now, with its facts.

item.description: The item id list_files, show_item or list_changes gave

device.description: This device's id: each name then says whether this device keeps it (kept), by the device's pin rules

tools.name: set_pin_rule
tools.description: Keep (or change) one pin rule: the items a device keeps on itself (a file's item, or a folder's item for everything under it).

device.description: The device the rule is for

items.description: The item ids to keep, from list_files, show_item or list_changes: a file's, or a folder's for everything under it

label.description: What the rule is, in the person's words

on.description: false keeps the rule but stops it applying; true by default

expected_version.description: The rule's version you read; 0 for a new rule

tools.name: remove_pin_rule
tools.description: Remove one pin rule at the version read.

tools.name: list_pin_rules
tools.description: One page of the pin rules, in id order, of one device or all.

tools.name: thumbnail
tools.description: A small picture of a file, at most size pixels on its longer edge, made once and kept under the file's content identity; thumbnail null with a reason when nothing makes one for its media type.

name_or_identity.description: A file's name (a path such as /Notes/a.mp4) or its content identity

tools.name: make_folder
tools.description: Make one folder inside a folder that exists, and answer its row (item, version, generation).

name.description: The new folder, a path such as /Notes/2026

expected_version.description: 0: nothing is at that name now (a name or folder already there is a conflict)

tools.name: bounds
tools.description: The numbers a caller sizes its calls by: page sizes, the most bytes a read, a span, a write and a piece carry, the stored chunk size, and the longest a store request waits for progress (idle_seconds).

tools.name: this_computer
tools.description: The computer this run is on: its id (the engine's id for it) and its label, as the engine filled them when it started the session; both null when the run was not started by the engine.

tools.name: tidy_propose
tools.description: Suggest a title and/or a folder for each of the person's files, each grounded in results already kept about the file (name them in evidence: a transcript, a summary). Each suggestion waits for the person to accept or reject it (tidy_list, tidy_decide); nothing is changed until tidy_apply. A title whose words the evidence does not mention, or a new folder it does not support, is refused.

name.description: The file's full name, starting with /

folder.description: The folder to move the file into, such as /Clients/Acme

evidence.description: The kinds of results kept for this file that the suggestion comes from

produced_by.description: Who suggested these (an AI app's name)

tools.name: tidy_list
tools.description: The suggestions for tidying the person's files, newest first, with how many are in each state (review, accepted, rejected, applied, stale, undone) and the tidy-up an undo would reverse.

tools.name: tidy_decide
tools.description: Accept or reject suggestions (the person's own choice) by their ids.

tools.name: tidy_apply
tools.description: Apply every accepted suggestion (or those of ids) as one named tidy-up: titles recorded, files moved into their folders. A file or evidence that changed since its suggestion is left out and marked stale. Undo it with tidy_undo.

tools.name: tidy_undo
tools.description: Undo a tidy-up (the newest when none is named): every file back to its name and title before, only when none changed since.

id.description: The tidy-up's id, as tidy_apply and tidy_history answer it

tools.name: tidy_history
tools.description: The tidy-ups applied, newest first, each with what changed for each file and whether undo would reverse it.

tools.name: retype_files
tools.description: Decide the type of each file that kept none (a missing or octet-stream type) from its first bytes and its name's ending, a page at a time from after. Answers how many were retyped and how many stayed unknown, and next_after: the id to resume after, or null when the last page is done.

after.description: The id the page starts after (the next_after of the last answer; left out for the first page)

limit.description: At most this many records, 1 to 1000
